problems.title: A quadratic in a squared expression
problems.question: Solve $(4x^2+12x+9)^2-3(2x+3)^2+2=0$.
problems.idea: Recognise the first inner polynomial as a square and substitute t for that square.
steps: Let $t=(2x+3)^2\ge0$. The equation becomes $(t-1)(t-2)=0$.
If t=1, then $2x+3=\pm1$, giving $x=-1,-2$.
If t=2, then $2x+3=\pm\sqrt2$, giving $x=(-3\pm\sqrt2)/2$.
All four values are real and satisfy their respective squared equations.

problems.title: Area of a quadrilateral around an incircle
problems.question: A quadrilateral has three consecutive side lengths $2,3,4$ cm and an incircle of radius $1.2$ cm. Find its area.
problems.idea: Tangency fixes the fourth side, and the area is inradius times semiperimeter.
steps: If the fourth side is d, then $2+4=3+d$, so d=3.
The perimeter is $2+3+4+3=12$, giving s=6.
The area is $1.2\cdot6=7.2$ square centimetres.

problems.title: Different completion times for two tractors
problems.question: Two tractors together complete $2/3$ of a job in four days. The second could complete the whole job five days faster than the first. Find their individual times.
problems.idea: Their combined rate is one-sixth of the job daily. Use reciprocal completion times.
steps: The combined daily rate is $(2/3)/4=1/6$.
Let the faster second tractor take t days, so the first takes t+5. Then $1/t+1/(t+5)=1/6$.
Clear denominators: $6(t+5)+6t=t(t+5)$, giving $t^2-7t-30=0$.
Factor: $(t-10)(t+3)=0$. Only positive time t=10 is valid.
problems.answer: First tractor: 15 days; second tractor: 10 days.

problems.title: Cancel factors without restoring forbidden inputs
problems.question: Solve $\frac{(x^2-1)(2-x)x}{(x^2-9x+14)(x-1)}\le0$.
problems.idea: Factor and simplify, but record the original denominator restrictions first.
steps: The original denominator excludes $x=1,2,7$.
On that domain the fraction is $-x(x+1)/(x-7)$. Thus solve $x(x+1)/(x-7)\ge0$.
The critical numbers are -1,0,7. The expression is negative on $(-\infty,-1)$, positive on $(-1,0)$, negative on $(0,7)$, and positive on $(7,\infty)$.
Include -1 and 0 because they make the numerator zero. Exclude 7. The other original exclusions 1,2 are already outside the selected intervals.

problems.title: Two angle bisectors and an area ratio
problems.question: In triangle ABC, the bisectors from A and C meet BC and AB at D and F respectively. Given $AB=21$, $AC=28$, $BC=20$, find $[ABC]:[AFD]$.
problems.idea: Each angle bisector supplies a side division. Areas then follow from the base fraction and height fraction.
formulas: For triangles with a common baseline, area ratios equal base times height ratios.
steps: From the A-bisector, $BD/DC=21/28=3/4$, hence $BD/BC=3/7$.
From the C-bisector, $AF/FB=28/20=7/5$, hence $AF/AB=7/12$.
As D moves along BC, its perpendicular distance to line AB is the fraction BD/BC of the distance from C to AB. Thus its height fraction is 3/7.
Therefore $[AFD]/[ABC]=(AF/AB)(BD/BC)=(7/12)(3/7)=1/4$.

problems.title: A difference of absolute values
problems.question: Solve $|x+1|-|x+2|\ge2x-3$.
problems.idea: Split at the inputs where either absolute value changes sign.
steps: If $x<-2$, the left side is $-(x+1)+(x+2)=1$. The inequality gives x≤2, automatically true in this case.
If $-2\le x<-1$, the left side is $-(x+1)-(x+2)=-2x-3$. The inequality becomes x≤0, automatically true in this interval.
If $x\ge-1$, the left side is $(x+1)-(x+2)=-1$. Then $-1\ge2x-3$ gives x≤1, so keep $[-1,1]$.
Combine the three intervals.

problems.title: Incircle radius from a trapezoid’s area
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid surrounds a circle and has area S. Its height is half its leg length. Find the incircle radius.
problems.idea: Tangency relates the bases to the legs; the incircle diameter is the height.
formulas: For equal legs of length l, tangency gives base sum $B+b=2l$.
steps: The leg is l=2h, so the bases sum to 4h.
Then $S=(4h)h/2=2h^2$. Thus $h=\sqrt{S/2}$.
The radius is half the height: $r=\frac12\sqrt{S/2}=\sqrt{S/8}$.

problems.title: When an absolute-value equation has two roots
problems.question: For which a does $|2x-a|=x+1$ have two distinct real solutions?
problems.idea: Solve both sign branches and check the conditions that make each branch valid.
formulas: The right side of an absolute-value equation must be nonnegative.
steps: On the branch $2x-a\ge0$, solve $2x-a=x+1$ to obtain $x=a+1$. Its branch condition is $a+2\ge0$, or a≥-2.
On the branch $2x-a\le0$, solve $-2x+a=x+1$ to obtain $x=(a-1)/3$. Its branch condition is again a≥-2.
For a=-2 the two formulas coincide at x=-1, so there is only one solution.
For a>-2 both candidates are valid and different. For a<-2 neither branch yields a valid candidate.

problems.title: Area of a trapezoid with two base angles
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has bases $AD=3a$, $BC=a$, with base angles $\angle BAD=30^\circ$, $\angle ADC=60^\circ$. Find its area.
problems.idea: The two horizontal leg projections add to the difference of the bases.
formulas: For height h and base angle θ, horizontal projection $=h\cot\theta$.
steps: The base difference is 2a. Thus $h\sqrt3+h/\sqrt3=2a$.
The coefficient is $4/\sqrt3$, so $h=a\sqrt3/2$.
The midline is $(3a+a)/2=2a$. Multiply by the height to obtain $S=2a\cdot a\sqrt3/2=\sqrt3a^2$.

problems.title: A parameterised quadratic with a simple factorisation
problems.question: For which a is the larger root of $x^2+(2a+1)x+a^2+a=0$ greater than 1?
problems.idea: The two roots differ by one and can be read from the factorisation.
steps: The roots are $-a$ and $-a-1$.
The larger is always $-a$.
Require $-a>1$, giving a<-1.
